decisions.issues: v11 (the only candidate) fails the script beat. Nagoji is on the left and matches his sheet and the ch3 row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, ochre rags, collar with side ring, manacles, bandaged wrists and a hobble chain. The pen chain runs from his fists up to the ring on its last bolt at the upper right, which is drawn well. The problem is that it then passes over Keshavrao's head and across his forehead and brow, so part of his face is covered. Keshavrao's fists close on nothing but the short chain between his own manacles, well below the pen chain. He is miming the pull, not hauling the pen chain with Nagoji. Minor points: no pen plank for their heels, and the pull runs sideways rather than toward the camera. Hands, feet, ankle irons and hobble chains are otherwise sound. There is no painted text, and the top-centre ceiling would give Nagoji's two lines room.
decisions.correction: Keep v11's hold: lantern light, dripping seams, shin-deep water, the splintered beam at the upper right with the ring hanging on its last bolt, Nagoji on the left and Keshavrao on the right, and both costumes, collars, manacles and hobble chains. Fix the chain path. The one pen chain runs from the ring at a shallow slant down into Keshavrao's two manacled fists, held in front of his belly at waist height, well below his chin. It then continues level through Nagoji's two fists, and its slack tail trails past Nagoji toward the lower-left foreground. Both men visibly close their fingers around the big pen-chain links themselves, not only their own short wrist chain. The pen chain never crosses or passes above either man's face or head: leave a clear gap of dark ceiling between the chain and Keshavrao's hair. Where the chain passes each man's collar ring, it hangs in a slack loop between collar and fists, so all the tension is on arms and shoulders and none is on the neck. Both lean back away from the ring with straight arms, heels dug against a heavy wooden pen plank that shows in the water at their feet. Keshavrao keeps a faint, thin young moustache, and neither man wears an ear stud except Nagoji. Keep the upper-centre ceiling between Nagoji's head and the chain dark and plain for two speech balloons.

decisions.issues: v13 is acceptable, with small issues. Nagoji matches his sheet and the ch3 bible row: thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud, long curly hair, torn ochre tunic, cream dhoti, bandaged wrists, collar with a side ring, wrist chain, ankle cuffs with a hobble chain, bare feet. His left forearm faces outward and the bandage hides the brand. He is braced at the rail, gripping a line, with a loose rope coil at his feet. The storm beat is clear: rain in sheets, lightning, a snapped mainmast leaning with torn canvas, a carved stern castle, barefoot mixed crew in loose shirts and slops, one sailor with a knife in his teeth, men heaving at pump handles. There are no oilskins, uniforms or coats, and no painted text (the carved stern panels are scrollwork only). There is no blood and no noose. Minor points: (1) Nagoji reads as slightly forward of the mast rather than aft, because the stern castle sits beyond the mast from this viewpoint. (2) The red-headcloth sailor's eyes drift toward the right and could be read as glancing at Nagoji. (3) Two small background sailors wear round brimmed hats, a period-plausible sailor's round hat and a cocked hat, not an anachronism. (4) No hatch is visible. There is clear sky for the two captions at the top left (about x 0.07-0.30, y 0.0-0.18, above the capped sailor's head) and the top right (about x 0.78-1.0, y 0.0-0.20, above the wave). Neither covers a face.

Acceptable, with minor points only. The computed task lists the cast as [nagoji] and only the CAPTION line. Script 1.2 and the ch03-r8 INDEX both have Keshavrao in the panel and give him the line "Storm." The frame correctly shows him on the right with the script's look: young, faint moustache, hacked short hair, grey-brown tunic, no stud, eyes up to the deck. If the letterer uses the script copy, his mouth is at about x 0.577, y 0.332, and the short balloon fits in the dark ceiling above and between the two heads (about x 0.47 to 0.60, y 0 to 0.12). Nagoji matches the sheet: thick curled moustache, clean chin with light captivity stubble, small round gold stud in the lobe, torn ochre sleeveless tunic that matches panel 1.1, bandaged wrists, hinged collar with a front ring, and eyes half closed. His anatomical left forearm, the one at the centre next to Keshavrao, is bandaged most of the way to the elbow, and its inner face is turned toward his body, so the brand stays hidden. It is not the ragged tunic flap that 1.1 asks for, but it meets the bible's rule that the arm is covered or turned from camera. The setting is the dim, lantern-lit wooden hold, with no sky and no guards, so it matches 1.1. There are no painted balloons, text, noose, blood or anachronism, and all four hands are sound. Minor points: the pen chain runs almost straight across at chest height through both collar rings instead of drooping in loops, though it is never vertical. The skin on Nagoji's shoulder shows a faint crosshatch texture from upscaling. The iron band on the left pillar has ornamental scrollwork, but none of it reads as letters. For the caption "Ships speak when they are in trouble.", the plain dark plank wall and ceiling at the right (about x 0.73 to 0.99, y 0.02 to 0.40) is the best spot, clear of both faces and all hands. A strip across the dhoti knees at the bottom (y 0.88 to 1.0) is a second option.
